threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still wait for a bus at the stop instead of just walking to your destination. Everyone else knows the best shortcuts through the estates.
Last night on the 196, a group of lads serenaded a pigeon outside Brixton Station. The bird looked more entertained than me.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The moment I spotted a wild cat sunbathing on my balcony while the BVG went on strike. Who knew urban life had such wild surprises?

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Berlin do you find people debating whether a bus will actually arrive during a strike, while sipping craft beer at the stop. It's a whole vibe!

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know someone’s from here when they know which BART station to avoid during a rainstorm. Civic Center's a no-go when the roof leaks.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a dog casually sunbathing on the Muni tracks today. Crew was trying to coax it off while commuters just smiled. Classic SF vibe.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think they can just stroll down Verdi for tapas, but locals know to hit up the hidden bars on Carrer del Sol for the real vibe.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell by their bewilderment at the winding streets—most locals navigate them like a second language, while newcomers clutch their maps.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: When you ask for a lemonade and get a confused look, only to find out they don’t serve anything that isn’t artisan or organic.
Last night on the 40, a couple were arguing over a bag of chips. The guy ended up throwing them out the window. Classic late-night drama.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: I was waiting for the bus on Sonnenallee and overheard a guy argue passionately about the best Döner in town. That's when it hit me—this is home.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg will you find a mural dedicated to a cat that lived in a specific yard for years—it's like a neighborhood mascot with its own street cred.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: True locals know that the sound of sirens means your brunch plans just went sideways. If they don't flinch, they're in it for the long haul.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy in a full tuxedo get off a Muni bus, take a quick selfie with a pigeon, then hop on a scooter. Only in SF.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Gràcia is just Gaudí and hipster bars. They miss the quiet corners where old ladies still gossip over daily groceries.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can always tell when someone’s new; they’re the ones who still look lost trying to navigate the L1 line on a Sunday.
